what_its_for: Fluorometholone is a steroid eye drop used to treat inflammation (redness, swelling, and irritation) in your eyes. It is commonly used after eye surgery or to treat certain eye conditions caused by allergies or injury.
how_to_take: Wash your hands thoroughly before using this medicine. Tilt your head back, pull down your lower eyelid to create a small pocket, and gently squeeze 1 drop into the pocket without letting the dropper touch your eye or any other surface. Close your eye gently for 1 to 2 minutes. If you wear contact lenses, remove them before using the drops and wait at least 15 minutes before putting them back in. If you are using the suspension (the liquid may look cloudy), shake the bottle well for about 10 seconds before each use.
dosing: The usual dose for adults is 1 to 2 drops in the affected eye(s) 2 to 4 times per day. Your doctor may tell you to use it more often at the start of treatment. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions, as the dose can vary depending on your condition.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, use it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not use extra drops to make up for a missed dose.
storage: Store at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C and 25°C). Keep the bottle tightly closed when not in use. Do not freeze. Keep out of reach of children. Throw away the bottle 4 weeks after opening, even if there is medicine left inside.
what_to_avoid: Do not touch the tip of the dropper to your eye, fingers, or any surface, as this can contaminate the medicine. Avoid wearing contact lenses while your eyes are inflamed or infected. Do not drive or operate heavy machinery right after using the drops if your vision is temporarily blurry. Avoid rubbing your eyes after using the drops.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you notice: new or worsening eye pain, sudden changes in your vision, increased redness or discharge from your eye, signs of eye infection (pus, swelling), headaches, or rainbow-colored halos around lights (this could be a sign of increased eye pressure). Also contact your doctor if your condition does not improve after 2 days of treatment.
when_it_works: You may start to notice some improvement in redness, swelling, or discomfort within a few days. However, it is very important to use all the medication for as long as your doctor tells you, even if your eyes feel better, to prevent the inflammation from coming back.
special_populations: Children: Safety and dosing in children under 2 years old has not been established. Use with caution in children and only as directed by a doctor. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding before using this medicine. Elderly: No special dose adjustments are typically needed for older adults, but regular monitoring of eye pressure is recommended during long-term use.
